idiom_name: sealed interface command hierarchy + exhaustive when + kotlinx.serialization discriminator
implementation_notes: Sealed interfaces/classes give a closed command set known at compile time, an exhaustive when expression replaces the abstract-command dispatch, and kotlinx.serialization writes the class discriminator (default key 'type', configurable per hierarchy) for polymorphic payloads - so the tag and the dispatch are compiler-checked and hand-written method-name strings disappear. Transport still comes from a client library (Spring, Kafka, JMS) or, in-process, from a Channel<Command> driven by a coroutine consumer. Use an open hierarchy (abstract class, no sealed) only when other modules must add commands.
pitfalls: kotlinx.serialization only writes the discriminator when the static type is the base class: serializing a concrete subclass omits 'type', and deserializing it later as the base fails.
A when over a sealed type is exhaustive only while all subclasses stay in the same module and package; moving one out turns a compile error into a runtime else/default path.
Blocking work inside a coroutine consumer occupies a dispatcher thread instead of the command's own context, which stalls unrelated commands on the same dispatcher.
